Tom manages the stable, reads his Bible, softens Miss Ophelia, and begins the conversion of Topsy

Eva distributes locks of her golden hair, pleads for freedom for 'our poor people,' and dies serenely

St. Clare received a fatal stab in the side with a bowie-knife while trying to separate two quarrelling men in a café
Marie sells off the servants; Tom is marched to the slave warehouse and sold at auction

Tom will not betray the women even under savage beating; 'I can die!'
Legree's rage results in Tom being beaten to death; Tom forgives and prays to the last
George Shelby arrives too late; kneels at Tom's side as he dies

The novel moves from parlors to steamboats, Quaker kitchens to swamps, showing how slavery corrodes masters but how people can choose to love and rescue
The night flight across the ice, Eva's farewell with locks of hair, the ghostly garret stratagem, and Tom's dying forgiveness are all rendered in the abridgment
Christian love expressed in cups of cold water, in refusing to flog, in Senator Bird bending the law to shelter Eliza
